label: rem:markov-trace-operator-construction
title: Markov-trace operator construction
html:
The Jones–Wenzl Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M : \mathbf{B}_\infty \to \mathbb{R} on the inductive limit of braid groups is uniquely characterised by the M1–M4 axioms (Jones 1985 / Wenzl 1988). One realises it as a single operator on the von Neumann inductive-limit hyperfinite \mathrm{II}_1 factor in five stages: a per-n Hilbert representation, an inductive embedding \iota_n : V_n \hookrightarrow V_{n+1}, the inductive limit V_\infty = \varinjlim V_n, the trace state on \bigcup_n H_n, and the bicommutant closure \mathcal{M} := (\bigcup_n H_n)''. On \mathcal{M}, the trace \mathrm{tr}_M provides the unique faithful normal trace up to scaling.

The per-n representation, the inductive embedding, and the GNS bicommutant factor hosting \mathrm{tr}_M are taken as hypotheses by the results downstream. The operator-algebra steps—the GNS state and the bicommutant closure—are what supply them for each n.

Archimedean specialisation. What follows sits on the archimedean side of the substrate wall. It invokes analytic constructs: real-valued physical observables, real-analytic bounds, transcendental constants, or numerical evaluation at the substrate parameter q_0. Generic categorical q-deformation identities remain valid over an abstract coefficient ring; one specialises only their archimedean realisation here.
